records.context: The statistic is the same but its input is not, although both are labelled "Gini". The Lorenz curves take raw gRNA counts pooled over a laboratory microplate; this panel takes each guide's share of its own well divided by that well's equal split. On the tsg101 screening experiment those are 0.20 and 0.32 -- the panel's is larger because normalising by the well removes the between-well spread that flattens the pooled curve. The two values are therefore not comparable.
records.label: spacr.figures.distributions.gini#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The statistic is the same but its input is not, although both are labelled "Gini". The Lorenz curves take raw gRNA counts pooled over a plate; this panel takes each guide's share of its own well divided by that well's equal split. On the tsg101 screen those are 0.20 and 0.32 -- the panel's is larger because normalising by the well removes the between-well spread that flattens the pooled curve. The two values are therefore not comparable.
records.translation: Tölfræðin er sú sama en inntakið ekki, þótt hvort tveggja sé merkt "Gini". Lorenz-ferlarnir taka hráar talningar gRNA sameinaðar yfir plötu; þetta spjald tekur hlutdeild hverrar leiðsagnarraðar í eigin brunni deilt með jafnri skiptingu þess brunns. Á tsg101-skimuninni eru gildin 0.20 og 0.32 -- gildi spjaldsins er hærra vegna þess að stöðlun eftir brunni fjarlægir dreifinguna milli brunna sem fletur út sameinaða ferilinn. Gildin tvö eru því ekki sambærileg.

records.source: THE EXPORTER IS THE ONE THE TABS USE. ``FastPlot._export_pdf`` and ``_export_svg`` are classmethods over a plot item, and both go through ``_paint_scene``, which turns pyqtgraph's export mode on for every mark before painting -- without it a ScatterPlotItem copies its cached marker PIXMAPS into the vector file, and a PDF full of little bitmaps of a dot is a PDF that claims to be vector and is not. Writing a second exporter here would recreate the same exporter duplication one level down.
records.translation: THE EXPORTER IS THE ONE THE TABS USE (útflytjandinn er sá sem fliparnir nota). ``FastPlot._export_pdf`` og ``_export_svg`` eru klasaaðferðir yfir ritatriði, og báðar fara í gegnum ``_paint_scene``, sem kveikir á útflutningsham pyqtgraph fyrir hvert merki áður en málað er -- án hans afritar ScatterPlotItem skyndiminnis-PIXMAPS merkja sinna inn í vigurskrána, og PDF fullt af litlum bitamyndum af punkti er PDF sem segist vera vigurskrá en er það ekki. Að skrifa annan útflytjanda hér myndi endurskapa sömu tvítekningu útflytjenda einu stigi neðar.

records.context: So a layer never says "row 40, column 12". records.context: **This module never deletes anything.** There is no call to ``deleteObjects`` in it, under any mode, for any object. If a previous ``APPEND`` run left three copies, ``REPLACE`` updates the oldest and *reports* the rest in :attr:`AnnotationResult.duplicates` — removing them is a decision for a human with the OMERO.web UI, not for an importer.

If a previous ``APPEND`` run left three copies, ``REPLACE`` updates the oldest and *reports* the rest in :attr:`AnnotationResult.duplicates` — removing them is a decision for a human with the OMERO.web UI, not for an importer.
records.translation: **Þessi eining eyðir aldrei neinu.** Ekkert kall á ``deleteObjects`` er í henni, í neinum ham, fyrir neinn hlut. Ef fyrri ``APPEND``-keyrsla skildi eftir þrjú afrit uppfærir ``REPLACE`` það elsta og *tilkynnir* hin í :attr:`AnnotationResult.duplicates` — að fjarlægja þau er ákvörðun fyrir manneskju með UI í OMERO.web, ekki fyrir innflutningstól.

records.context: **TagAnnotations are never edited.** In OMERO a tag is a *shared* object; renaming the tag linked to this image renames it on every other object in the group that carries it. So :func:`export_tag_annotation` links a tag when the verdict is new, does nothing when the identical verdict is already linked, and reports the previous tag when the verdict has *changed* — it never unlinks and never renames.

records.context: The import is written as ``importlib.import_module(OMERO_GATEWAY_MODULE)`` rather than as a literal ``import omero.gateway`` for that same reason: the one place the name is resolved is a named constant next to the guard that checks what came back, instead of a bare statement in a file of the same name. That blind spot is pinned from the other side by ``tests/test_omero.py::test_omero_py_is_reached_through_a_string_literal_and_must_not_be_removed``, so a dependency audit does not report omero-py as unused.

records.context: Everything that is easy to get wrong here is *arithmetic and string formatting*, not RPC: the row/column mapping, the filename, the id parsing, the float formatting, the decision to replace rather than append. All of it lives in pure functions over plain data — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — and the ``BlitzGateway`` calls are confined to a thin layer that only walks containers and moves bytes. This module is therefore tested on a machine with no OMERO server and no ``omero-py`` installed: the fake gateway in ``tests/test_omero.py`` implements about a dozen methods, and everything worth testing is reachable through it.
records.label: spacr.omero#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Everything that is easy to get wrong here is *arithmetic and string formatting*, not RPC: the row/column mapping, the filename, the id parsing, the float formatting, the decision to replace rather than append. All of it lives in pure functions over plain data — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — and the ``BlitzGateway`` calls are confined to a thin layer that only walks containers and moves bytes. This module is therefore tested on a machine with no OMERO server and no ``omero-py`` installed: the fake gateway in ``tests/test_omero.py`` implements about a dozen methods, and everything worth testing is reachable through it.
records.translation: Allt sem auðvelt er að gera rangt hér er *reikningur og strengjasnið*, ekki RPC: vörpun raða/dálka, skráarheitið, þáttun auðkenna, snið fleytitalna, ákvörðunin um að skipta út frekar en bæta við. Allt þetta býr í hreinum föllum yfir einföld gögn — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — og köllin á ``BlitzGateway`` eru afmörkuð við þunnt lag sem aðeins fer um ílát og flytur bæti. Þessi eining er því prófuð á vél án OMERO-netþjóns og án uppsetts ``omero-py``: gervitengingin í ``tests/test_omero.py`` útfærir um tylft aðferða, og allt sem vert er að prófa er aðgengilegt í gegnum hana.
